title: Brain Myths You Probably Still Believe
desc: Left-brain people, a hidden ninety percent, learning styles, the Mozart effect, letting off steam and memory like a camera: tonight we gently check six popular ideas about the brain against the research, and see why such myths feel so true. A calm, sourced look at what the studies actually found.
plan: b01: intro list; neuromyths; left-brain/right-brain (Sperry, Nielsen 2013); ten percent myth (Beyerstein 1999, Raichle & Gusnard 2002)
b02: learning styles (Dekker 2012, Pashler 2008, Roediger & Karpicke 2006); Mozart effect (Rauscher 1993, Pietschnig 2010, Thompson 2001)
b03: venting (Breuer & Freud 1895, Bushman 2002 and 1999); memory as camera (Simons & Chabris 2011, Loftus & Palmer 1974, Loftus & Pickrell 1995)
b04: why myths stick (Hasher 1977, Fazio 2015); correcting them (Lewandowsky 2012, Skurnik 2005); takeaways, callback, calm close, end
